question: outcome_summary
answer: The Urdu ASQ demonstrated strong psychometric properties with a sensitivity of 94.2% and specificity of 73.9%. The negative predictive value was 97.7%, while the positive predictive value was 52.0%. The overall screen-positive rate was 41.7%, with significant variations based on age and medical setting. The study underscores the prevalence of suicidal ideation and the necessity for validated screening tools in non-English languages.

question: demographics_summary
answer: The study included 300 individuals aged 15 to 45 years, with a nearly even gender distribution: 158 females (52.7%) and 142 males (47.3%). The mean age was 21.7 years (SD = 9.4). Participants were categorized into three age groups: 15-17 years (19.7%), 18-25 years (28.7%), and 26 years and older (51.7%).
